title: Once an orphan, so do not crush the orphan
translation: Did He not find you an orphan and give you shelter? He found you wandering and guided you; He found you in need and made you rich. So do not crush the orphan, and do not drive away the one who asks.
body: What was **ḍāll**? **Ibn Kathir**: “unaware” of scripture (cf. 42:52); Jalalayn: “erring” from the Law; Maududi denies any error of creed. Verses 9–10 turn the Prophet’s past into duty, as **Deuteronomy** turns Israel’s slavery into care for the orphan. For **Luther**, one freely helped becomes “a sort of Christ” to the neighbour.
question: Does ḍāll in 93:7 mean unaware of revelation, lost, or in error? Which does the wording favour?
source_label: Ibn Kathir, Jalalayn, Maududi on 93:7 · Luther, Freedom of a Christian (1520)
